hook.text: Its first cover idea showed Marvin the Martian aiming a raygun at Earth, until legal trouble ruled it out.

facts.label: Recorded
facts.value: August to October 1985, Chicago Recording Company

facts.label: Players
facts.value: Steve Albini (guitar, vocals, drum machine programming), Santiago Durango (guitar), Dave Riley (bass guitar)

sentences.text: Atomizer was Big Black's first full-length album.
Before it came out, 'Big Money' was the B-side of the 'Il Duce' single.
Homestead also put 'Big Money' and 'Il Duce' on a promo record with three live songs, under an agreement that it be used only for promotion.
The label sent it to radio stations, then sold extra copies outside Chicago, and the band found out.
The band left Homestead and signed with Touch and Go.
Dave Riley was new to the band for this album, and Andy Kellman called his bass lumberjack-like.
The credits list Roland alongside the band members, though Roland is a drum machine brand and not a person.
The following year the band recorded the four-song Headache EP, and its sticker warned buyers that it fell short of Atomizer.
That same year, Atomizer was put on CD with the Headache EP and the 'Heartbeat' single, under the title The Rich Man's Eight Track Tape.
The CD left off 'Strange Things', which a later reissue restored, and had none of the original artwork or liner notes.
Steve Albini used the CD's liner notes to say he disliked the format, and told readers to scratch the discs and eat sandwiches off them.
In May 2011 St. Vincent played a live cover of 'Kerosene' at Bowery Ballroom in New York.

listen_for.text: Andy Kellman says its guitar intro cannot be accurately described by imitating it with your voice or with gestures.
Its guitar work has been described as warped beyond recognition.
Andy Kellman believes it may be a reply, perhaps unintended, to John Mellencamp's 'Pink Houses'.
